bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at `libxml2/tree.c:3828` while `xsltFuzzXslt` parsed the exact staged 3949-byte XML witness with `xmlReadMemory(data, size, NULL, NULL, 0)`. The one-line file declares XML 1.1 with `encoding="TSCII"`, defines internal entity `a`, places one `&a;` in document content, and also embeds another `&a;` inside `a`'s replacement text. That makes `xmlParseReference` re-enter `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` on the same entity body. The nested replacement text contains malformed multi-colon tag names, so `xmlParseQName` takes the fallback branch at `libxml2/parser.c:8826` and interns the current QName in the parser dictionary via `xmlDictLookup`; the saved ASan allocation stack roots the crashing address at `xmlDictAddString` -> `xmlDictLookup` -> `xmlParseQName`. `xmlSAX2StartElementNs` then builds a new element node that carries that dict-backed `localname`, but static inspection of the staged witness shows 267 `<` bytes and zero `</` end tags, while `xmlParserMaxDepth` is 256. `nodePush()` therefore returns -1 on the excessive-depth guard, and `xmlSAX2StartElementNs` immediately runs `xmlUnlinkNode(ret); xmlFreeNode(ret);`. `xmlFreeNode` reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` and ASan reports the resulting bad-free of the interior dictionary pointer. The staged libxslt patch only removes deprecated direct `xmlXPathInit()` calls, so it is at best an indirect fix artifact for this reproduced parse-side crash path.

source.description: First project-code consumption of the attacker buffer on the witnessed path. The fuzz helper hands the exact staged XML bytes to libxml2's DOM parser.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 3949-byte one-line XML 1.1 document declaring `encoding="TSCII"`, defining internal entity `a`, and containing two `&a;` tokens: one recursive reference inside the entity body and one reference in document content. Static inspection of the staged file also shows 267 `<` bytes and zero `</` sequences, which is enough to drive deep start-element nesting during `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)`.
source.note: This is the scored source boundary. The AFL/libFuzzer entry point only forwards the buffer here and is intentionally omitted from the causal fine trace.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `xmlFreeNode` loads `dict = cur->doc->dict` and then reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`, which ASan shows falls through to `free()` on a pointer from libxml2's dictionary pool.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports the bad-free at this exact line. Source shows that `DICT_FREE` only calls `xmlFree` when `cur->doc->dict` is NULL or `xmlDictOwns` returns 0; runtime disambiguation is disabled for this sample, so the exact predicate failure is left to the ASan evidence linking the freed address back to `xmlDictAddString` / `xmlDictLookup` / `xmlParseQName`.

root_cause.description: Depth-error cleanup unlinks and frees the just-created element node after `nodePush()` fails, routing a partially constructed node that still carries the parser-dictionary QName into generic node destruction.
root_cause.note: The staged source proves that the node's `name` came from `xmlParseQName` and that `xmlUnlinkNode` in this cleanup does not clear `ret->doc`; `xmlFreeNode` therefore evaluates `DICT_FREE` against the same document pointer carried by the node. With runtime disambiguation disabled, the GT does not over-assert which ownership sub-predicate failed inside `DICT_FREE`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete pointer later freed at the sink. `xmlParseQName` interns the current malformed multi-colon QName in the parser dictionary and returns the dict-backed string.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved ASan allocation stack reports the crashing address as a pointer inside a 4048-byte dictionary allocation from `xmlDictAddString` reached through this `xmlDictLookup` in `xmlParseQName`.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the value-provenance anchor for the later bad-free: ASan ties the address freed at the sink back to this dictionary lookup, while the fine trace separately narrows the later ownership check itself.

parser_admitted.description: The exact staged witness is handed from the libxslt fuzz helper into libxml2's XML parser. Stage 01 crashes inside this call before stylesheet compilation or transformation starts.

document_dict_attachment.description: Because `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)` does not set `XML_PARSE_NODICT`, `xmlCtxtUseOptionsInternal` leaves `ctxt->dictNames = 1` and the outer document parser attaches its dictionary to `ctxt->myDoc` before document content and entity expansion are parsed.

recursive_entity_expansion.description: The witness contains two `&a;` tokens, so the document-content reference to entity `a` recursively re-enters balanced-chunk parsing on `a`'s own replacement text.

depth_guard.description: Static inspection of the staged witness finds 267 `<` bytes and zero `</` sequences, while `xmlParserMaxDepth` is 256, so the excessive-depth guard on the witnessed path is reachable without speculative OOM assumptions.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact staged XML bytes are parsed with `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)`, so libxml2 directly processes the recursive internal entity `a` and the malformed nested start-tag stream carried in the witness.

Expanding `&a;` in document content recursively parses `a`'s own replacement text in a fresh parser context that reuses the outer document and dictionary state; inside that recursive parse, malformed multi-colon tag names reach `xmlParseQName` and are interned in the shared parser dictionary.
With `ctxt->dictNames` still enabled, the new element node keeps the dict-backed QName pointer and stores the current `ctxt->myDoc` document pointer that `xmlFreeNode` later consults for ownership.
Because the witness contains more start-element openings than the default parser depth allows, `nodePush()` trips the `xmlParserMaxDepth` guard and returns an error for the current node.

The depth-error cleanup unlinks the partial node without clearing its `doc` field, then `xmlFreeNode` loads `dict = cur->doc->dict` and reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`; ASan shows that this invocation falls through to `free()` on the dictionary-backed QName.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact staged 3949-byte XML witness is parsed directly from attacker-controlled memory. Its internal subset defines entity `a`, its body recursively contains `&a;`, and the whole file contains 267 `<` bytes with no `</` sequences, which together drive the later recursive depth-error path.

When document content reaches the witness `&a;`, libxml2 parses the replacement text of internal general entity `a` as a balanced chunk. Because the staged file also embeds another `&a;` inside that replacement text, this same balanced-chunk parser is re-entered recursively on the attacker-controlled entity body.

Recursive balanced-chunk parsing drops the fresh parser dictionary, reuses the outer parser dictionary, reuses the outer document because `oldctxt->myDoc` is already live during document-content entity expansion, and restores the outer `dictNames` flag. Combined with the earlier `xmlSAX2StartDocument` document-dictionary attachment, later node creation and free in this recursive parser run against that same outer doc/dict pair.

fine_trace.code:
tmp = xmlBuildQName(tmp, l, NULL, 0);
l = xmlDictLookup(ctxt->dict, tmp, -1);
fine_trace.note: Inside the recursive entity text, malformed multi-colon start-tag names drive `xmlParseQName` through its fallback branch, which interns the current QName in the reused parser dictionary from step 3. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies the crashing address as a pointer allocated by this `xmlDictLookup` via `xmlDictAddString`.

With `ctxt->dictNames` still enabled, the new element keeps the dict-backed `localname` from step 4 instead of duplicating it. Both creation paths also stamp the node with `ctxt->myDoc`, so the `cur->doc` later seen by `xmlFreeNode` comes from this recursive parser state.

The witness keeps opening nested elements from the recursive entity body without matching closes. Since the staged file has 267 `<` bytes, zero `</` bytes, and `xmlParserMaxDepth` is 256, `nodePush()` takes the excessive-depth guard and returns `-1` rather than a memory-allocation failure.

Root cause. After step 6 rejects the current nesting level, `xmlSAX2StartElementNs` immediately unlinks and frees the just-created node. `xmlUnlinkNode` only detaches parent and sibling links, so the node reaches `xmlFreeNode` still carrying the same `doc` pointer from step 5 and the same dictionary-backed `name` from step 4.

fine_trace.code:
if (cur->doc != NULL) dict = cur->doc->dict;
...
if ((cur->name != NULL) &&
    (cur->type != XML_TEXT_NODE) &&
    (cur->type != XML_COMMENT_NODE))
    DICT_FREE(cur->name)
fine_trace.note: Sink. `xmlFreeNode` first derives `dict` from `cur->doc->dict`, then evaluates `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` for the node from step 7. The staged source proves which `cur->doc` is consulted and that the freed name pointer came from step 4, but it does not statically reveal whether this witness fell through because `dict` was NULL or because `xmlDictOwns(dict, cur->name) == 0`; with runtime disambiguation disabled, that final ownership-test outcome is grounded by the ASan crash and allocation stacks.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch removes deprecated direct `xmlXPathInit()` / `xmlInitMemory()` calls from libxslt, but Stage 02 did not run the fixed version and the reproduced Stage 01 crash chain is visible entirely inside libxml2's parse-side depth-error cleanup. The patch is therefore only indirect grounding for this specific witness path.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is a parser-dictionary string from `xmlDictAddString` / `xmlDictLookup` / `xmlParseQName`. The source trace shows that recursive entity parsing reuses the outer parser document/dictionary, `xmlSAX2StartElementNs` preserves that dict-backed name on the new node, the depth-error cleanup passes that node into `xmlFreeNode`, and ASan is the evidence that `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` fell through to `free()` for the witnessed address.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the exact 3949-byte one-line XML 1.1 file consumed by `xsltFuzzXslt` through `xmlReadMemory(data, size, NULL, NULL, 0)`. Its verified trigger facts are source-level and witness-specific: it declares `encoding="TSCII"`, defines internal entity `a`, contains one `&a;` in document content and another inside the entity body itself, and carries enough malformed nested start-tag text to make `xmlParseReference` recursively enter `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal`, make `xmlParseQName` intern a malformed QName at line 8826, and then make `nodePush()` hit the excessive-depth cleanup in `xmlSAX2StartElementNs`.

format.name: One-line XML 1.1 stylesheet text for tests/fuzz/xslt
format.contract: Exactly the staged `poc` file as parsed by `xsltFuzzXslt` with `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)`. The verified trigger is not generalized beyond this witness: it must preserve the recursive internal general entity `a`, the malformed multi-colon QName bytes that reach `xmlParseQName`'s fallback-dictionary path, and the start-tag-heavy structure (267 `<` bytes and zero `</` sequences in the staged artifact) that makes `nodePush()` exceed `xmlParserMaxDepth = 256`. Those exact source-grounded facts are what drive the dict-backed QName pointer from `xmlParseQName` into the `xmlSAX2StartElementNs` -> `xmlFreeNode` bad-free.
